title: Reading the Count: Prediction Markets and Brazil's 2026 Presidential Election
abstract: arXiv:2611.00338v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We rebuild the public count of Brazil's 2026 presidential runoff minute by minute from the electoral court's section-level records and compare it with every trade on Kalshi and Polymarket. A projection published live on the night gave the eventual winner, Lula, a probability of 0.998 from 19:15, with 1.6% of sections counted. The markets reached 0.9 at 20:24, with 46% counted. Read as the projection's central estimate with a wider uncertainty, their prices imply a standard deviation of the final margin about four times the live projection's, and about twice that of a section-level projection calibrated on the 2018 runoff, the earlier night with the largest errors. Valued at these projections, takers' purchases of Lula after the count resumed had an expected profit of 4 to 18 cents per Kalshi contract after fees; valued at a state-level extrapolation of the count, it was zero. translated_title: 解读计票：预测市场与巴西2026年总统选举
translated_abstract: 我们根据选举法院的分区级记录逐分钟重建了巴西2026年总统决选的公开计票结果，并将其与Kalshi和Polymarket平台上的每一笔交易进行对比。当晚实时发布的一项预测从19:15起（在仅统计1.6%选区时）就给出了最终获胜者卢拉0.998的获胜概率，而市场直到20:24、统计了46%的选区时才达到0.9。若将市场价格理解为带有更大不确定性的预测中心估计，其价格意味着最终票差的标准差约为实时预测的四倍，也约为基于2018年决选（此前误差最大的夜晚）校准的分区级预测的两倍。按这些预测估值，在计票恢复后，交易者购买卢拉合约在扣除费用后每份Kalshi合约的预期利润为4至18美分；而按计票结果的州级外推估值，预期利润则为零。在计票暂停的两小时内，市场给卢（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究逐分钟重建巴西2026年总统决选计票并与预测市场交易对比，发现实时统计预测远比Kalshi和Polymarket更快、更准确地锁定卢拉的胜选，市场价格隐含的不确定性约为预测的四倍，且据预测估值存在明显的套利空间。
en_tdlr: By rebuilding Brazil's 2026 presidential runoff count minute by minute and comparing it with every Kalshi and Polymarket trade, this study shows that live statistical projections identified Lula's victory far earlier and with much greater precision than prediction markets, whose implied uncertainty was roughly four times larger and whose mispricing offered exploitable arbitrage opportunities.
